title: CENTCOM: formation of 12 metallic orbs skimming the ocean

tellings.quote: >> Central command discusses cuboid formation of metallic orbs on USG networks.

plain: About twelve metallic orbs were filmed in tight formation, skimming the ocean at high speed in the area covered by the US military's Central Command, according to the so-called Immaculate Constellation report. The report has no signature. A man named Michael Shellenberger delivered it to Congress, and Representative Nancy Mace entered it into the record of a House Oversight hearing on 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon. It calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department. A former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown later said he wrote it, and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. Under the heading "CENTCOM Cuboid Formation of Metallic Orbs," which Michels reads out on an episode with Brown, the report describes "a formation of ~12 metallic orbs skimming the ocean surface at high-speed before dispersing in multiple directions," flying at first "in a tight 'cuboid' formation". So the count of twelve is the report's rough figure, and the footage is described in words, not shown.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report's case "CENTCOM Cuboid Formation of Metallic Orbs" describes footage of "a formation of ~12 metallic orbs skimming the ocean surface at high-speed before dispersing in multiple directions", flying at first "in a tight 'cuboid' formation". Jesse Michels reads out the heading, so the twelve orbs are the report's approximate count, from footage it describes in words and does not show.
